analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. No executable code, keys, attestation or authorization logic is in the supplied units, so the changes cannot alter controls themselves. The two supplied head units (inference.md lines 2033-2603) are unchanged context. The changed ranges are lines 810-813, 829 and 1896-1899, which are not visible in the supplied text. I could only read their patch excerpt, and it is truncated at the inline video labels bullet. The cli-reference.md metadata unit has no text, and its patch at line 52 is fully visible.

The documented behavior change is that GLM5Next video now accepts variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate instead of being refused with a 400. The CLI doc also references inline video labels in `MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders`.

If the corresponding Swift change landed, the relevant surface is the media-ingest path on the consumer-controlled input side. This falls under TB-007/TB-003 and T-050 (video plaintext temp files) and the memory admission gates. Those controls are documented as unchanged: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap, the 25 MiB encoded cap, the 600 s duration limit, the 384 Mpx per-request frame pixel cap, and in-memory assets with no disk write. Media requests stay excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so the T-041 cross-tenant cache surface is not widened.

Open integration question: the actual Swift implementation of VFR frame indexing is not in this batch. The next pass should check that the VFR path keeps the frame, duration and memory caps, does not write the payload to disk, and does not let a mismatched nominalFrameRate inflate the sampled frame count or the decode-time work. No security regression is established from the docs alone. I am not asserting that the code is safe.
